title: A Bengaluru thrift marketplace killed 'fake seller' fear and 3x'd repeat buyers by spending on trust before scaling ads
content: SITUATION: A Bengaluru pre-loved fashion app had 14,000 installs but a brutal 1.4% buyer conversion and AOV of just ₹740. Exit surveys (1,200 responses) named the real blocker: 68% feared 'item won't match the photos' or 'the seller is fake' — classic resale trust collapse. The leak compounded downstream — returns ran at 22%, refund fights clogged WhatsApp support, and repeat purchase was a weak 11%. We were buying distrustful cold users on Meta at ₹90 CAC and then losing them. ACTION: We froze broad Meta prospecting and moved that budget into a trust engine. Every listing now needed a 90-second condition-grading video (front, back, flaw close-up); sellers earned a 'Verified Closet' badge tied to Aadhaar plus 3 completed sales; and we shipped a '₹0-risk 48-hour return' promise pushed in-app and over WhatsApp. We seeded 40 micro-thrift creators (8k-25k followers, ₹3,500/post) running live haul-and-try-on sessions for honest UGC instead of polished ads. OUTCOME: Over 4 months conversion rose 1.4%→4.6%, returns fell 22%→9%, repeat purchase jumped 11%→33%, and WhatsApp re-engagement flows lifted AOV ₹740→₹980. Blended CAC settled at ₹78 (down from ₹90) — the win was conversion, not cheaper clicks.
lesson: In resale, trust IS the funnel, not a feature you bolt on later. Distrust shows up twice — as low conversion AND high returns — so optimising ad creative alone just buys skeptics faster and bleeds money on refunds. Spend on verification, brutally honest condition proof, and a real return safety net BEFORE scaling paid. And micro-creators doing live try-ons sell trust far cheaper than any prospecting ad: the creator's face is the warranty.
